metadata.description: Blend: shows that sit between two others (/blend, and the link on show pages).
Universes: franchise timelines, watch order and links (/universes, and the section on show pages).
Essential cut: the shorter way through a long show (/shows/{id}/essential-cut, and the teaser on show pages).
Tonight's plan: episodes that fit the time and mood given (/tonight, and its links on Home and Up Next).
Reunion radar: shows where actors from shows you love work together again (/reunions, and its link on For you).
Show DNA: the trait profile on show pages. Recommendations use DNA either way.
Forecasts: the What's next panel on show pages, and Will you finish it? on show pages and Stats.
Nanogenres: chips on show pages, /nanogenres browse pages, and the search filter. Recommendations use them either way.
DNA twins: shows made like this one but about something else, on show pages.
When it gets good: the section on show pages, the nudge in Will you finish it?, and the Worth the wait discovery list.
Creator fingerprint: a creator's signature style, shows made their way and kindred creators, on person pages.
TV time machine: /time-machine (this week in TV history, or any date's week), its teaser on Home and link on Insights.
Does it stick the landing?: the section on ended shows' pages, and the Great endings discovery list.
Previously on…: a rewatch refresher on the show page after a long break, and the Back after a break list on Up Next.
Catch-up planner: a week-by-week plan to be caught up before a followed show's new season, on the show page and Up Next.
Is it worth going back?: for dropped shows, whether what's left gets better, on the show page and the backlog.
Backlog triage: /backlog ranks followed shows not started by how much they're worth your time, with verdicts.
Fits your time off: /time-off suggests finished shows to watch start to end in the hours you have.
Spoiler shield: a setting that hides titles, summaries and stills of episodes you haven't watched.
Social: following people, the activity feed (/feed), people pages and search.
Tonight for two: plan an evening with someone you follow (/tonight?with=…) from the shows you share.
Community insights: viewers' tips on show and episode pages, ranked by how many found them helpful.
Corrections: viewers suggest fixes to show and episode data; moderators accept them into the catalog.
Where do I know them from? On a show's cast, the other shows the user has watched each actor in.
Holiday episodes: Halloween, Thanksgiving, Christmas, New Year's and Valentine's episodes of the user's shows and across the catalog.
Title formulas: shows whose episode titles follow a pattern (Friends' "The One…", Stranger Things' "Chapter…").
Characters' names: TV characters who share a first name, the most common names, and each name by decade.
Cast ages: each main cast member's age at a show's latest episode, who grew up on screen, and the youngest and oldest casts.
Between seasons: each show's waits between seasons, and the longest waits, revivals and shows still waiting.
Episode lengths: how long a show's episodes run season by season, and the shows that grew or shrank most.
TV atlas: where your shows are set, on a world map, and where each show is set on its page.
Your TV clock: when you watch, what kind of viewer that makes you, and your sittings.
Who said it?: a quiz of lines from episodes you've watched.
Memorable lines: quotes from Wikiquote on show and episode pages.
Spoiler watch: how exposed you are to spoilers for your shows right now, and when it calms down.
Where the cast went next: on a show page, each main cast member's roles since the show ended (or started).
Your TV life: every year of your life with the biggest premieres and finales, and what you watched.
Six degrees: the shortest chain of shared actors between any two shows, and a challenge to beat.
Call it: predict a season's rating before it premieres, and see whether you beat the forecast model.
Guess the show: a daily puzzle, one popular show found in six guesses with clues.
Season verdict: how a season that just ended did, on show pages, on Insights and as a notification to followers.
Character trail: every show where an actor plays the same character, in air order, with your progress, from the show page's cast.
Episode notes: moderators mark episodes essential or skippable with a source on the research page, and the essential cut follows them.
The "Watch on Netflix" button on show pages, linking to the show on its streaming service.
Crossover alerts: a notification when a crossover across a followed universe's shows is near, and "Crossover ahead" on Up Next with what to catch up on first.
Weekly digest: one email a week, at the user's day and hour, instead of an email per alert; its setting and preview in Settings.
Taste twins: anonymous people whose ratings track yours, and what they loved that you haven't seen (5-user rule).
Awards shelf: awards from saved research on show pages, and Prestige picks: the most-awarded shows you haven't started.
Network report cards: how each network's and streamer's shows rate, end, come back and how long they keep you waiting.
Episode duels: rank a show's episodes you've watched by picking the better of two.
Waiting room: shows you're caught up on, with when they're back (scheduled or forecast).
Mixtape: pick three shows and get the shows that fit all of them.
Your services (Plus and Family): pick the streaming services you pay for and see each one's cost per hour watched; also the logos and prices on network report cards.
Family plan: the owner invites up to 5 people by link, and each gets Plus's benefits from the one subscription.
List links: a list's owner makes a link anyone can open, signed in or not, showing the list read-only.
Plans: Free and Plus. Free accounts get 3 lists and can't share them; off, nobody has a limit. Also the plan page and admins' plans page.
Is it worth it?: a 0-100 score on show pages, with the parts behind it, and the Worth your time discovery list.
Year in TV: a personal recap of a year's viewing, from your own watches, ratings and follows.
Ask the app: questions about shows answered by the local model with the app's MCP tools (signed in).
Research: moderators enrich a show from Wikidata, Wikipedia, TMDB and pasted pages, with a model-drafted insight; the saved research shows on the show page and overrides catalog fields.
